title: The PCP Assessment: Diagnose, Pick a Protocol, Reassess

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already size up the scene, do a primary survey, take a history and do a rapid trauma exam. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Form a working diagnosis fast and spot priority patients
  2. Add the BC functional enquiry and match findings to a protocol
  3. Reassess on schedule, with PCP targets for glucose and head injury

Textbook: Chapter 17, PDF pages 1495–1569
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter seventeen. At its core, patient assessment is the same for an EMR and a PCP: scene, primary survey, history, exam and reassessment. You've done it many times, so today we focus on what changes. A PCP doesn't just collect findings; you turn them into a working diagnosis, choose a protocol, and prove it's working. We'll cover three things: forming a working diagnosis fast and spotting priority patients; the functional enquiry, which BC requires from PCPs only; and reassessment on a schedule, with the PCP targets for glucose and head injury.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第十七章。患者评估的核心，EMR 和 PCP 是一样的：现场、初检、病史、体检、复评。你们已经做过很多次了，所以今天只讲变化在哪里。PCP 不只是收集发现，而是要把它们变成工作诊断、选定流程，并证明处置有效。今天讲三件事：快速形成工作诊断并识别优先患者；BC 只要求 PCP 做的系统问诊；以及按时间表复评，包括 PCP 在血糖和颅脑外伤上的目标值。

slides.title: Your first 90 seconds
slides.body:
Scene→Initial→Focused→Detailed→Ongoing
  • Initial assessment: 60–90 seconds to find and fix life threats
  • Start a working diagnosis now; confirm or reject it later
  • Mental status = best single marker of severity
  • GCS: report E, V and M separately, not just the total
  • Snoring → reposition; gurgling → suction
  • 10 × 500 mL = 5,000 mL beats 24 × 200 mL = 4,800 mL
slides.say: You know the flow. In the first sixty to ninety seconds, you look, talk and touch, and you start a working diagnosis, a best guess that the rest of your assessment will confirm or reject. Mental status is your best single marker of how sick someone is. With the Glasgow Coma Scale, report the eye, verbal and motor scores separately, because the same total can hide very different patients. Snoring means reposition; gurgling means suction. And fast isn't the same as enough: ten breaths of five hundred millilitres move more air than twenty-four breaths of two hundred.
slides.sayZh: 流程你都熟悉。在最初六十到九十秒里，你边看、边问、边摸，同时开始形成工作诊断，也就是一个最佳猜测，后面的评估会证实或推翻它。意识状态是判断病情轻重最好的单一指标。用格拉斯哥昏迷评分时，睁眼、言语、运动三项要分开报告，因为同样的总分背后可能是很不一样的病人。打鼾声就调整体位，咕噜声就吸引。还有，呼吸快不等于够：每次五百毫升呼吸十次，比每次两百毫升呼吸二十四次换的气更多。

slides.title: Priority patients: limit scene time
slides.body:
• Poor general impression; unresponsive or can't follow commands
  • Difficulty breathing; hypoxia not fixed within 1–2 minutes
  • Shock; uncontrolled bleeding; severe pain anywhere
  • Chest pain, SBP < 100 (BC: any cardiac chest pain); suspected stroke
  • Complicated birth; abdominal injury; multiple injuries, severe burns
  • Severe hypertension

Essentials only on scene; the rest en route. BC exam goal: ready to load in 15 min.
slides.say: Part of those first ninety seconds is deciding whether this is a priority patient. The book's list includes a poor general impression, a patient who is unresponsive or can't follow commands, difficulty breathing, low oxygen that doesn't correct within one to two minutes, shock, uncontrolled bleeding, severe pain, chest pain with a systolic under one hundred, suspected stroke, a complicated birth, abdominal injuries, multiple injuries or severe burns, and severe high blood pressure. On the BC exam, any suspected cardiac chest pain counts as unstable, whatever the pressure. For these patients, do only the essentials on scene; the BC goal is ready to load within fifteen minutes. As a PCP, most of your extra skills, like the IV, belong in the ambulance.
slides.sayZh: 最初九十秒里还要判断：这是不是优先患者。书里的清单包括：总体印象差；无反应或不能听从指令；呼吸困难；一到两分钟内纠正不了的低氧；休克；未控制的出血；剧痛；胸痛且收缩压低于一百；疑似卒中；复杂分娩；腹部受伤；多发伤或严重烧伤；以及重度高血压。在 BC 考试中，只要怀疑是心源性胸痛，不论血压多少都算不稳定。对这些病人，现场只做必要的处置；BC 的目标是十五分钟内做好装载准备。作为 PCP，你多出来的大部分技能，比如开静脉，都应该在救护车上做。

slides.title: Secondary survey: four patient types
slides.body:
PatientYour main tool
Responsive medicalHistory drives it; exam targets the complaint
Unresponsive medicalFull head-to-toe, monitor, SpO₂, ETCO₂, glucose; 2+ sets of vitals
Trauma, significant MOIRapid trauma exam, 2–3 minutes, DCAP-BTLS
Trauma, isolated injuryFocused exam; low BP means look further

The detailed exam takes 15+ minutes: do it en route on longer transports.
slides.say: Your approach depends on the patient. For a responsive medical patient, the history does most of the work, and the exam targets the complaint. For an unresponsive medical patient, you lose your best source, so do a full head-to-toe exam and use your tools: the monitor, oximetry, capnography and the glucometer, with at least two sets of vital signs. Trauma with a significant mechanism gets a rapid trauma exam, about two to three minutes. An isolated injury gets a focused exam, but if that patient is hypotensive, something bigger is going on. The detailed exam takes fifteen minutes or more, so do it en route.
slides.sayZh: 做法取决于病人类型。清醒的内科病人，主要靠病史，体检针对主诉。无反应的内科病人，你失去了最好的信息来源，所以要从头到脚全面检查，并用上工具：心电监护、脉氧、呼气末二氧化碳和血糖仪，至少测两组生命体征。有重大受伤机制的创伤病人，做快速创伤评估，大约两到三分钟。孤立伤做重点检查，但如果这个病人血压低，说明还有更严重的问题。详细体检需要十五分钟以上，放到转运途中做。

slides.q: Which patient is a priority patient who needs a short scene time?
options: Ankle sprain, good distal pulses, pain 4/10
Small forearm cut, bleeding controlled, normal vitals
Mild nausea for an hour, normal vitals
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. Which patient is a priority patient who needs a short scene time? A, an ankle sprain with good distal pulses and pain four out of ten. B, chest pain with a blood pressure of ninety-four over sixty and a pulse of one hundred eighteen. C, a small forearm cut, bleeding controlled, with normal vitals. D, mild nausea for an hour, with normal vitals. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：哪一位是需要缩短现场时间的优先患者？A 踝关节扭伤，远端脉搏好，疼痛四分；B 胸痛，血压九十四比六十，脉搏一百一十八；C 前臂小伤口，出血已控制，生命体征正常；D 轻度恶心一小时，生命体征正常。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Chest pain with a systolic under one hundred, especially with a fast pulse, means the heart is struggling, and it's on the priority list. As a PCP, note the drug angle too: BC lists a systolic under one hundred ten as a contraindication to nitroglycerin. A, C and D are stable, with reassuring findings, so they can have a full assessment on scene.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。胸痛且收缩压低于一百，尤其还伴心跳快，说明心脏在挣扎，属于优先患者清单。作为 PCP，还要注意用药的角度：BC 把收缩压低于一百一十列为硝酸甘油的禁忌证。A、C、D 都是稳定的病人，发现都让人放心，可以在现场做完整评估。

slides.title: From findings to a BC protocol
slides.body:
Your findingsBC protocol
Wheezes; asthma or COPD historySOB with asthma/COPD
Crackles, JVD, ankle edema; heart failureCHF / pulmonary edema
Blood or fluid loss, SBP < 90, shock signsHypovolemia
Low LOC, no known causeDiabetic emergencies (BGL first)
Slow, shallow breathing; pinpoint pupilsSuspected narcotic overdose
Head trauma + altered LOCTraumatic brain injury
slides.say: This is the core PCP skill: turning findings into a protocol. Wheezes in a patient with asthma or COPD lead to the shortness of breath protocol. Crackles, swollen neck veins and ankle edema in a heart failure patient lead to the CHF and pulmonary edema protocol. Blood or fluid loss with a systolic under ninety and other signs of shock leads to hypovolemia. A lowered level of consciousness with no known cause sends you to diabetic emergencies, starting with a glucose check. Slow, shallow breathing with pinpoint pupils suggests a narcotic overdose. And head trauma with any altered level of consciousness means a traumatic brain injury.
slides.sayZh: 这是 PCP 的核心技能：把发现变成流程。哮喘或 COPD 病人有哮鸣音，走气短流程。心衰病人有湿啰音、颈静脉怒张和脚踝水肿，走心衰/肺水肿流程。有失血或失液、收缩压低于九十、并有其他休克征象，走低血容量流程。意识水平下降、原因不明，走糖尿病急症流程，第一步就是测血糖。呼吸慢而浅、瞳孔针尖样，提示阿片类过量。头部外伤加上任何意识改变，就按颅脑外伤处理。

slides.title: Glucose: check it when LOC drops
slides.body:
• Built-in glucose check: diabetic, narcotic overdose, stroke protocols
  • Heat illness with lowered LOC: glucose is in the first vitals
  • BC hypoglycemia: BGL < 4.0 mmol/L, every age
  • All levels: oral glucose if airway protected; EMR: glucagon if not
  • PCP: D10W 10–25 g IV (100–250 mL); glucagon if no IV
  • Then recheck glucose and level of consciousness
slides.say: Low sugar can imitate almost anything: a stroke, drunkenness, a seizure. Several BC protocols build in a glucose check: diabetic emergencies, suspected narcotic overdose and stroke; and in heat illness with a lowered level of consciousness, glucose is part of the first vital signs. In BC, hypoglycemia means a reading under four point zero millimoles per litre, at any age. Every licence level can give oral glucose if the patient can protect the airway; if not, the EMR gives glucagon. The PCP instead starts an IV and gives D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, which is one hundred to two hundred fifty millilitres, and uses glucagon only if there's no IV. Then recheck.
slides.sayZh: 低血糖几乎什么都能模仿：卒中、醉酒、抽搐。好几个 BC 流程都内置了测血糖：糖尿病急症、疑似阿片类过量和卒中；中暑病人如果意识下降，血糖也属于第一组生命体征。在 BC，低血糖指读数低于四点零毫摩尔每升，不分年龄。所有级别都可以给口服葡萄糖，前提是病人能自己保护气道；如果不能，EMR 给胰高血糖素。PCP 则是建立静脉通路、给 D10W：十到二十五克，也就是一百到二百五十毫升；建不了静脉才用胰高血糖素。之后要复测。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the functional enquiry
slides.body:
BC assessment model, secondary survey: the functional inquiry is marked PCP required.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • History
  • Vital signs
  • Head-to-toe exam

PCP adds

  • Functional enquiry: questions by body system
  • 9 systems on the BC grading sheet
  • EMRs don't do it
slides.say: Here is the clearest difference between EMR and PCP assessment in BC. In the BC assessment model, the secondary survey for every licence level includes the history, vital signs and a head-to-toe exam. The PCP adds one more piece: the functional enquiry, which BC marks as PCP required. It's a structured set of questions, organized by body system, that can uncover problems the chief complaint doesn't reveal. EMRs don't do it. Think of it as a head-to-toe done with questions: the exam checks each system with your hands, and the functional enquiry checks each system with your words.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 里 EMR 和 PCP 评估最明显的区别。在 BC 评估模型中，所有级别的二次评估都包括病史、生命体征和从头到脚的体检。PCP 多一项：系统问诊（functional enquiry），BC 标明为 PCP 必做。它是一套按身体系统组织的结构化提问，能发现主诉本身没有暴露的问题。EMR 不做。可以把它想成「用提问做的从头到脚检查」：体检用手查每个系统，系统问诊用话问每个系统。

slides.title: The nine systems, and the scoring
slides.body:
The 9 systems on the BC grading sheet
General health · Central nervous system · Respiratory
Cardiovascular · GI/GU · Integumentary (skin)
Musculoskeletal · Endocrine · EENT
  • System not asked: −5%
  • Asked, but missed info pertinent to the complaint: −3%
  • Missed info not pertinent: −1%
  • Capped at 15% in total
  • No deduction if unresponsive or no history available
slides.say: The BC grading sheet lists nine systems: general health; central nervous system; respiratory; cardiovascular; GI and GU, meaning the gut and the urinary and genital tract; integumentary, which is the skin; musculoskeletal; endocrine, the hormone glands, as in diabetes; and EENT, eyes, ears, nose and throat. Here's the scoring. A system you don't ask about costs five percent. Asking but missing information pertinent to the chief complaint costs three percent. Missing information that isn't pertinent costs one percent. The whole enquiry is capped at fifteen percent, and there's no deduction if the patient is unresponsive or no history is available.
slides.sayZh: BC 评分表列出九个系统：一般健康状况；中枢神经系统；呼吸系统；心血管系统；GI/GU，也就是消化道和泌尿生殖道；皮肤系统；肌肉骨骼系统；内分泌系统，也就是激素腺体，比如糖尿病；以及 EENT，眼、耳、鼻、喉。评分方法如下：一个系统没问，扣百分之五；问了但漏掉与主诉相关的信息，扣百分之三；漏掉与主诉无关的信息，扣百分之一。整个系统问诊最多扣百分之十五；病人无反应或无法获得病史时不扣分。

slides.q: On your BC practical exam, you're the PCP for a chest pain patient. You've done the primary survey, a full history using OPQRRRST, vital signs and a head-to-toe exam. What is still missing from your secondary survey?
options: Nothing: the secondary survey is complete
A functional enquiry by body system
A tilt test before any treatment
A full 15-minute detailed exam on scene
slides.say: Let's try an exam question. On your BC practical exam, you're the PCP for a chest pain patient. You've done the primary survey, a full history using OPQRRRST, vital signs and a head-to-toe exam. What is still missing from your secondary survey? A, nothing; it's complete. B, a functional enquiry by body system. C, a tilt test before any treatment. D, a full fifteen-minute detailed exam on scene. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道考试题。BC 实操考试中，你是一位胸痛病人的 PCP。你已经做了初检、用 OPQRRRST 问完了完整病史、测了生命体征、做了从头到脚的体检。你的二次评估还缺什么？A 什么都不缺，已经完整；B 按身体系统的系统问诊；C 任何处置前先做倾斜试验；D 在现场做完整的十五分钟详细体检。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. In the BC assessment model, the PCP's secondary survey adds a functional enquiry across nine body systems, and each system you skip costs five percent, up to fifteen percent in total. For chest pain, cardiovascular and respiratory questions are clearly pertinent. A would be true for an EMR, not a PCP. C isn't a required step, and D belongs en route on a long transport, not on scene with chest pain.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。在 BC 评估模型里，PCP 的二次评估多了覆盖九个身体系统的系统问诊，漏问一个系统扣百分之五，最多扣百分之十五。对胸痛病人来说，心血管和呼吸系统的问题显然是相关的。A 对 EMR 成立，对 PCP 不成立；C 不是必做步骤；D 应该在长途转运时于途中做，而不是胸痛病人还在现场时做。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: head injury targets
slides.body:
BC TBI protocol: head trauma + any altered LOC. GCS ≥ 13 mild · 9–12 moderate · ≤ 8 severe

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if needed
  • Head of the bed up 30°
  • Loosen the hard collar

PCP adds

  • Blood glucose 4.0–8.0 mmol/L
  • Systolic BP > 120 mmHg
  • IV at TKVO if systolic is above 120
  • No TXA for an isolated TBI
slides.say: Head injury is where PCP reassessment has hard targets. BC grades a traumatic brain injury by GCS: thirteen or more is mild, nine to twelve moderate, and eight or less severe. Every licence level keeps the saturation at ninety-four or above, assists breathing if needed, raises the head of the bed to thirty degrees and loosens the hard collar. The PCP adds targets: keep the glucose between four and eight, keep the systolic above one hundred twenty, and run the IV at TKVO, to keep the vein open, when the systolic is above one hundred twenty. Why so strict? The book notes that one episode of low blood pressure can double the death rate in a serious brain injury.
slides.sayZh: 颅脑外伤是 PCP 复评有硬指标的地方。BC 按 GCS 给颅脑外伤分级：十三分及以上为轻度，九到十二为中度，八分及以下为重度。所有级别都要维持血氧九十四以上、必要时辅助通气、床头抬高三十度、松开硬颈托。PCP 多了几个目标：血糖维持在四到八之间；收缩压维持在一百二十以上；收缩压高于一百二十时，静脉以 TKVO（保持静脉通畅）的速度滴注。为什么这么严格？书里指出，严重脑外伤只要出现一次低血压，死亡率就可能翻倍。

slides.title: Ongoing assessment: how often, what
slides.body:
• Stable: about every 15 min; unstable: every 5 min
  • Repeat: mental status, ABCs, vitals, lung sounds, focused exam
  • Check each intervention: did it do what you expected?
  • Priority patients: at least 3 sets of vitals, usually 4–5
  • Revise the plan: step transport up, or down if stable

BC IV maintenance: reassess the patient and the IV every 5–15 minutes.
slides.say: After the initial assessment, the ongoing assessment is the most important one you'll do, and you repeat it until handover: about every fifteen minutes for stable patients, every five for unstable ones. Each round, recheck mental status, the ABCs, vital signs, lung sounds and your focused exam, then check each intervention: did it do what you expected? After a fluid bolus for bleeding, for example, you'd expect the pressure to rise and the pulse to slow. Priority patients need at least three sets of vital signs, usually four or five. BC's IV maintenance guideline agrees: reassess the patient and the IV every five to fifteen minutes.
slides.sayZh: 在初检之后，持续评估是你做的最重要的评估，要一直重复到交接为止：稳定病人大约每十五分钟一次，不稳定病人每五分钟一次。每一轮都要复查意识状态、ABC、生命体征、呼吸音和重点检查，然后核对每一项处置：效果是否符合预期？比如给出血病人补液之后，你预期血压上升、脉搏变慢。优先患者至少要测三组生命体征，通常四到五组。BC 的静脉维护指引也一致：每五到十五分钟复评一次病人和静脉通路。

slides.title: Trends that should alarm you
slides.body:
TrendMeans
Pulse slows, BP rises, breathing irregularCushing reflex: rising intracranial pressure
Narrow pulse pressure, muffled heart sounds, JVDBeck triad: cardiac tamponade
Heart rate keeps climbingOngoing bleeding, hypoxia, or a failing heart
SpO₂ falling, patient tiringRespiratory failure is close

A bad trend = change the plan: upgrade priority, notify, treat.
slides.say: Serial vital signs show patterns that one set never shows. A slowing pulse, rising blood pressure and irregular breathing together are the Cushing reflex, a grave sign of rising pressure inside the skull. A narrowing pulse pressure, muffled heart sounds and swollen neck veins form Beck's triad, meaning cardiac tamponade, usually after penetrating chest trauma. A heart rate that keeps climbing means ongoing bleeding, low oxygen or a failing heart. Falling saturation in a patient who's tiring means respiratory failure is close. When you see a trend like these, change your plan: upgrade the priority, notify the hospital, and treat.
slides.sayZh: 系列生命体征能显示出单组读数看不到的规律。脉搏变慢、血压升高、呼吸不规则同时出现，是库欣反射，提示颅内压升高，是危重征象。脉压变窄、心音遥远、颈静脉怒张构成 Beck 三联征，意味着心脏压塞，通常发生在胸部穿透伤之后。心率持续上升，说明还在出血、缺氧或心脏衰竭。越来越疲惫的病人血氧在下降，说明呼吸衰竭快来了。看到这类趋势就要改变方案：提升优先级、通知医院、给予处置。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A working diagnosis is a hypothesis: change it if findings disagree
  • Hypovolemia: vascular access en route, or on scene only if delayed
  • Stroke, abdominal and chest trauma: vascular access en route
  • Low LOC? Check glucose before blaming alcohol or stroke
  • Oxygen: titrate to 94% unless SOB, shock or CO poisoning
  • A worsening complaint = hidden cause or failing treatment
slides.say: Now the new watch-outs. First, your working diagnosis is a hypothesis; if the reassessment doesn't fit, change it. Second, timing. BC puts PCP vascular access en route: for hypovolemia, en route or if there's a delay, and for stroke, abdominal injuries and chest trauma, en route. Third, in anyone with a lowered level of consciousness, check the glucose before you blame alcohol or a stroke. Fourth, more oxygen isn't always better: BC titrates to ninety-four percent unless the patient is short of breath, in shock or has carbon monoxide poisoning. And fifth, a complaint that gets worse means a hidden cause or a failing treatment.
slides.sayZh: 新的注意事项如下。第一，工作诊断只是假设；复评结果对不上，就修改它。第二，时机。BC 把 PCP 的静脉通路放在转运途中：低血容量是途中或有延误时，卒中、腹部外伤和胸部外伤都是途中。第三，意识水平下降的病人，先测血糖，再考虑是醉酒还是卒中。第四，氧气不是越多越好：BC 按百分之九十四调节，除非病人气短、休克或一氧化碳中毒。第五，主诉在加重，说明有隐藏的病因，或者处置没有起效。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Pain: BC uses OPQRRRST or LOTARP (book: OPQRST)
  • Also scored: past history, medications, allergies, last oral intake
  • Lungs: at least 6 anterior or 6 posterior points
  • Book's chest decompression: not on the BC exam; an ACP skill in BCEHS
  • Open chest wound: occlusive dressing; lift a corner if tension develops
  • EMRs have no IV access: vascular access is a PCP skill
slides.say: Some BC points for your exams. For pain, BC's scoring sheets expect OPQRRRST or LOTARP, where the book uses OPQRST, so practise one BC version out loud. The rest of the history is scored too: past history, medications, allergies and last oral intake. For the lungs, BC wants at least six points on the front or six on the back. The book mentions decompressing the chest for a tension pneumothorax, but needle decompression isn't on the BC licensing exam; in BCEHS it's an ACP skill. For an open chest wound, use an occlusive dressing, and if signs of tension develop, lift a corner to let the air out. And remember, vascular access is a PCP skill; EMRs don't have it.
slides.sayZh: 几个 BC 考点。问疼痛时，BC 评分表要求用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP，而书里用 OPQRST，所以要把其中一个 BC 版本练到能脱口而出。病史的其他部分也计分：既往史、用药、过敏和最后进食。听肺时，BC 要求前胸至少六个点，或后背至少六个点。书里提到为张力性气胸做胸腔减压，但 BC 执照考试不考针刺减压；在 BCEHS，它属于 ACP 技能。开放性胸部伤口用封闭敷料；出现张力征象时，掀开一角放气。还要记住，静脉通路是 PCP 的技能，EMR 没有。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. First 90 seconds: working diagnosis + priority; PCP extras go en route
  2. PCP secondary survey adds the functional enquiry; findings → protocol
  3. Reassess every 5–15 min; check glucose; TBI: SBP > 120, BGL 4.0–8.0

Next: Chapter 18, Clinical Decisions
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: in your first ninety seconds, form a working diagnosis and decide if this is a priority patient; if it is, your PCP extras go en route. Two: your PCP secondary survey adds the functional enquiry across nine body systems, and your findings should lead you to a specific protocol. Three: reassess every five minutes if unstable and every fifteen if stable, check the glucose whenever consciousness drops, and in head injury keep the systolic above one hundred twenty and the sugar between four and eight. Next, Chapter eighteen: clinical decisions. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，最初九十秒里形成工作诊断，并判断是不是优先患者；如果是，PCP 的额外处置放到途中做。二，你作为 PCP 的二次评估多了覆盖九个身体系统的系统问诊，你的发现应该把你引向一个具体的流程。三，不稳定病人每五分钟、稳定病人每十五分钟复评一次；意识下降就测血糖；颅脑外伤要让收缩压保持在一百二十以上、血糖在四到八之间。下一课是第十八章：临床决策。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
